questions.question: During the driving test, what should you do at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is going too slow.
Get out of the vehicle to check for a train.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: Is it okay to fuel a bus while passengers are on board?

options.text: Yes, but only at night.
Yes, but only on trips longer than 100 miles.
Yes, but only if it is absolutely necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, but only if it is absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not fuel a bus while passengers are on board unless you must. Never fuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: What can buses carry?

options.text: Small arms ammunition.
Corrosive materials.
Poison gas.
Explosives other than small arms ammunition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Small arms ammunition.
questions.explanation: Buses can carry small arms ammunition labeled ORM-D, emergency hospital supplies, and drugs. Most other hazardous materials cannot be carried on buses.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of drowsiness?

options.text: Frequent blinking
Drifting from your lane
Feeling hungry
Yawning

questions.correctAnswerText: Feeling hungry
questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include frequent blinking, eyes closing by themselves, frequent yawning, and drifting between lanes. Feeling hungry is not a sign of drowsiness.

questions.question: How should a pre-trip inspection be done?

options.text: It should be done differently each time.
It should be done in the same order every time.
It should only be done on sunny days.
It should not be done if the vehicle seems fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be done in the same order every time.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-trip inspection the same way every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you do not miss anything.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Stop on the tracks.
Change gears.
Try to pass another vehicle.
Stay in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on the railroad tracks.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you need to stop before turning, what should you do?

options.text: Skid to a stop.
Stop after the stop line to see better.
Let your vehicle roll.
Keep your front wheels aimed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your front wheels aimed straight ahead.
questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind any stop line, crosswalk, or sign. Keep your front wheels straight and do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: If your brakes pull to one side when you use them, what does this mean?

options.text: The brakes are working properly.
The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes are new.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, you have a brake problem. Fix it before driving. It is illegal to drive an unsafe vehicle.

questions.question: How can you best avoid cell phone distractions while driving?

options.text: Stay on one call for the entire trip.
Turn the phone off before driving.
Only accept incoming calls.
Use the phone to text instead of talk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the phone off before driving.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid cell phone distractions is to turn your phone off before you start driving and keep it off until you arrive.

questions.question: If there are no gates or lights at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because the tracks are probably abandoned.
Park and walk to the tracks to check for trains.
Look both ways down the tracks for approaching trains.
Do what the other vehicles around you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look both ways down the tracks for approaching trains.
questions.explanation: At a crossing with no gates or lights, look in both directions down the tracks to make sure no trains are coming before you cross.

questions.question: After you stop during the stop/start maneuver, you should:

options.text: Apply the parking brake.
Keep the vehicle in first gear.
Park parallel to the curb.
Block a driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: When you park during the stop/start maneuver, you must apply the parking brake. Put the gear in neutral or park. Park parallel to the curb. Do not block driveways or intersections.

questions.question: How should you put out an electrical fire?

options.text: Use water.
Use a B:C extinguisher.
Use an X extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a B:C extinguisher.
questions.explanation: Use a B:C fire extinguisher for electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: While driving, a driver should:

options.text: Ignore what is happening on the sides of their vehicle.
Pay attention to all sides of the vehicle.
Ignore what is happening behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention to all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always be aware of what is happening on all sides of your vehicle. Look ahead at the road and check your mirrors regularly on both sides while driving.

questions.question: While driving, car gauges should be:

options.text: Ignored because they are unreliable.
Ignored because they are unpredictable.
Watched for warning signs of trouble.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watched for warning signs of trouble.
questions.explanation: Watch your gauges while driving to spot any warning signs of problems. Check your gauges before you start driving to make sure they work properly.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, which of these is NOT something you should check?

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure.
Tires with excessive wear.
Tires made by different manufacturers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different manufacturers.
questions.explanation: Check that your tires have at least 4/32 inch tread depth on the front and 2/32 inch on other tires. Make sure tires are not worn, cracked, or over-inflated, and that they are all the same size.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The trailer detaches from the truck.
The vehicle becomes easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: When it rains, your tires can lose traction and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph.

questions.question: To warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down, you can:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Tap the brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
Turn on one set of turn signals.
Put your hand out the window and wave.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tap the brakes lightly a few times before slowing down.
questions.explanation: Before you slow down, lightly tap your brake pedal a few times. This flashes your brake lights and warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: In an emergency while driving, you should:

options.text: Always stop.
Not always stop.
Never swerve.
Always turn on your flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not always stop.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest choice in an emergency. It is often safer to steer away from danger to avoid a crash.

questions.question: In very hot weather, you should check your tires regularly because:

options.text: They may melt.
Air pressure increases as temperature rises.
The tread wears down faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure increases as temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Heat causes tire air pressure to increase. Pay close attention to your tire pressure and condition when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: An accident on the roadway.
An open road.
A police car helping a motorist on the side of the road.
An ice cream truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: An open road.
questions.explanation: An accident can distract drivers passing by. Ice cream trucks are hazardous because children may run into the road without watching for cars. Police cars on the roadside can also distract drivers.
